newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt pondering private-sector water projects.
newsitem.headline: Egypt pondering private-sector water projects.

text.p: An Egyptian ministry wants to bring the private sector into water and sewerage projects, the government newspaper al-Ahram said on Friday.

The Ministry of Housing and New Communities has identified at least 73 projects where the private sector could build and manage water and sewerage services and will put its plan to the cabinet at its next meeting, it said.

Water supply and sewerage have been state monopolies for decades, with the exception of a small water desalination plant for hotels in south Sinai, and officials have not previously mentioned these as areas open to the private sector.

"The programme will for the first time allow the private sector to set up, manage and operate water and sewerage plants at prices to be fixed and approved by the government," al-Ahram said, quoting Housing Minister Mohamed Ibrahim Soleiman.
The projects include some in three new cities in the desert -- Tenth of Ramadan City and Sixth of October City near Cairo and Burg al-Arab near Alexandria, it said.
"If the cabinet approves the programme, it will be promoted locally and in the Arab world... The ministry is setting the rules and conditions for accepting the companies," it added.
It did not specifically say that non-Arab foreign companies would not be eligible to carry out such projects.
Last year Egypt took the first steps towards opening new airports, roads and some electricity projects to the private sector under BOT (build-operate-transfer) formulae.
The most advanced is Marsa Alam airport on the Red Sea coast, where the government has selected a Kuwaiti company for detailed negotiations on the project.
